Portfolio Spotlight: Hex Security (YC W26) Most companies still rely on periodic penetration testing. But software now ships continuously, and the gap between audits is often where vulnerabilities emerge. In mid-September 2025, Anthropic detected a Chinese state-sponsored cyber-espionage campaign that used AI to automate 80 to 90% of attack activity, with the system making thousands of requests, often multiple per second. Hex Security builds AI agents that run continuous penetration testing across applications, APIs and infrastructure. Instead of relying solely on annual testing, Hex’s agents operate 24/7 to find vulnerabilities, chain exploits and deliver verified findings with reproduction steps. The company is founded by Ahmad Khan , who previously worked on robotics and World Models; Huzaifa Ahmad , who previously built software at PlayAI, AWS and Capital One; and Prama Yudhistira , who previously worked on coding agents at Codegen and GPU firmware testing infrastructure at AMD. Hex Security was one of 12 companies we selected from Y Combinator's Winter 2026 batch. We're proud to back Hex Security alongside Jeremy Hindle , as part of the W26 cohort. We’re publicly expanding the types of data Datoric can collect from the physical world after completing pilots. We’re now collecting UMI gripper, tactile, and dexterous hand data, capturing trajectories, grasp states, contact forces, tactile feedback, and other signals for robotic manipulation and dexterity. At the same time, we’re continuing to expand our voice data capabilities across 50+ languages. We’re building the infrastructure to capture more of the real world, across speech and physical interaction.
